parent.behavior_scope: accepted system-level direct failure and repair control

source.source_boundary: Traditional FRT at both system and installed LRU is 300000 per million OPHOURS, so one item contributes the full system failure rate. A failed LRU is removed in a system SURP repair, replaced from one local stock item, then directly repaired at the same WS via ItemRepair. StockAllocation STSIZ declares nominal stock; native evidence must establish the opening on-hand quantity. ISTOH applies to reorder positions and is unused here.

delta.mechanism: Redirect the accepted system failure clock to one installed critical LRU; local spare replacement takes 0.5 h and removed LRU direct repair takes 1.0 h.

predeclared_native_acceptance: The frozen seed/configuration must produce at least one observed installed-LRU failure, with time read from native events rather than prescribed in advance.
Import/export must preserve all nonblank source business rows, conversion errors must be zero, and all four native CLI steps must succeed.

For each observed failure, trace LRU identity through mission impact, system SURP task and spare demand, local issue, REMOVE and REPLACE, system recovery, removed-item DIRP task, repair completion and local restock; reconcile stock on hand and outstanding demand at each transition.
Compare mission and system results to the accepted system-direct D01 control, explaining any differing stochastic event times or recovery interval.
Use session-0 SSH under the host-wide native queue, preserve GUI PID 13340, seal raw hashes and obtain independent read-only replay.
limits: This covers one installed LRU, one local spare and a local direct ItemRepair path only; no remote supply, shortage, multiple removals, explicit task breakdown, PM, resource competition or alternate failure mode is accepted.
Exact stochastic timestamps and event sequence are evidence from the observed native run, not guarantees inferred from the seed.
ItemRepair.DIRPT and SystemRepair.SURPT are total turnaround times, not measured wrench time.
